title: Add rule for fs
Add system dependencies for geospatial Python packages (GDAL, PROJ, e…
description:
This pull request adds essential system libraries required to deploy geospatial Python packages (e.g., `geemap`, `geopandas`, `pyproj`) via `reticulate` in a Shiny app. These include:

- `libgdal-dev`
- `libproj-dev`
- `libspatialindex-dev`
- `libgeos-dev`
- `g++`
- `python3-dev`

These dependencies are critical for a dashboard we’re building at the BC Centre for Disease Control to integrate Google Earth Engine, chlorophyll-a modeling, and public health monitoring across British Columbia. 
Thanks for considering this addition!

title: remove the debian imagemagick default policy file
description:
@dcaud kindly [opened another PR](https://github.com/rstudio/shinyapps-package-dependencies/pull/321) to adjust the imagemagick policy to enable larger amounts of memory to be used.

After working through the changes required, looking at [imagemagick policy docs](https://imagemagick.org/script/security-policy.php) and having a side conversation with @jeroen about the expectations I think it's best to instead remove the policy altogether.

When magick support was [first added](https://github.com/rstudio/shinyapps-package-dependencies/commit/cc4b25f1a0c87c08dc9fb78409cfa7d12736d44f) to shinyapps.io, the policy installed by the debian package was [far less restrictive](https://salsa.debian.org/debian/imagemagick/-/blob/ca7fe0456001c891bf074890dc3b920154c95ecf/config/policy.xml) (eg. it was not really restrictive at all). Over time, and mainly with our upgrade to focal for these images, the policy has become significantly restrict to account for security and cpu concerns in the generic debian install cases. These cases are not really applicable to the sandboxed-based environments of shinyapps.io and it seems fruitful to put policy needs and desired into the hands of shinyapps.io application deployers, rather than here.

This PR removes the file, and allows imagemagick to make use of its default, non-restrictive, policy for all values.

title: there is no R package named openbabel
Use `pak` when package installation is not found
description:
Fixes #234

This PR is to get the conversation going to hopefully remove maintenance requirements of shinyapps.io by offloading to `pak` which uses RSPM to query [rstudio/r-system-requirements](https://github.com/rstudio/r-system-requirements)

## Benefits:
* Unify the installation patterns
* Stop playing wack-a-mole on installations failures that are defined elsewhere
* From https://github.com/rstudio/r-system-requirements readme:  
> This metric indicates how good the rules are for the majority of packages R users are likely to install
> Ubuntu 18
> No rules 90.1%
> With rules 99.2%".

## Setup: 
* If there is **no** install script, then `pak` is used.
  * This PR does not use the CRAN version of `pak`. Instead, it uses the hosted version provided by RStudio's `r-lib` team. This is done to update rapidly as bug fixes are found. I'd recommend moving to a CRAN installation once the dev version makes it to CRAN.
  * Disadvantage: This requires RSPM to work / function, whereas the static files are known at install time.
* If there is a package install script, the install script is used.
  * Using the existing install script will **not** install dependencies for the required packages. I do not know which packages are supplied at install time. Ex: `rgl` originally only wanted to install `libgl1-mesa-dev` and `libgl-mesa-dev`, where `pak` says it requires:
```
❯❯ pak::pkg_system_requirements("rgl", "ubuntu", "18.04")
 [1] "apt-get install -y imagemagick"      "apt-get install -y libmagick++-dev"  "apt-get install -y make"
 [4] "apt-get install -y libicu-dev"       "apt-get install -y pandoc"           "apt-get install -y libfreetype6-dev"
 [7] "apt-get install -y libglu1-mesa-dev" "apt-get install -y libpng-dev"       "apt-get install -y libgl1-mesa-dev"
[10] "apt-get install -y zlib1g-dev"
```




## Alterations:
* I have removed simple installation files that immediately matched ubuntu 18.04. If there were more complicated ones, like `sodium`, I did not remove their install script.
* I am working on making a GitHub Action to test all known packages. (bionic && xenial)


## Future:
Game plan moving forward. I'd recommend spamming the few handful of authors for packages like `av` which require system installations, but do not report them so that `rstudio/r-system-requirements` picks them up automatically. (Curious as to why `av` by Jeroen doesn't have any `pak` sys reqs when its `SystemRequirements` looks like: `FFmpeg (>= 3.2); with at least libx264 and lame (mp3) drivers. Debian/Ubuntu:libavfilter-dev, Fedora/CentOS: ffmpeg-devel (via https://rpmfusion.org), MacOS Homebrew: ffmpeg.`)

title: add packages websocket & pagedown support
description:
Hi,

Following [this question](https://community.rstudio.com/t/error-after-using-pagedown-to-generate-a-pdf-from-html-in-a-shinyapp/45999?u=rlesur) on RStudio Community, here is a PR to add the support for the [pagedown](https://cran.r-project.org/package=pagedown) package on shinyapps.io.

I've locally tested against xenial and bionic.

I want to warn you that I had to add a Pandoc installation step to pass a basic functional test. I was surprised because I thought that Pandoc was already installed on shinyapps.io. Tell me if I must remove this step.

Another point: pagedown depends on the websocket package.  
For the bionic image, the websocket package installation failed because `libssl-dev` was not installed.
For the xenial image, the websocket package was correctly installed.

The change creates a "whitelist" of supported distributions and only adds the repo if its a supported distro for that machine.

title: Fix redland and tesseract tests failing on unreachable hosts
description:
`make test-jammy-redland` and `make test-jammy-tesseract` were both failing. Neither failure was a problem with the packages or their system dependencies — both were network problems in the test scripts.

## redland

This was the only package still installing from `http://cran.us.r-project.org`. That host now redirects to `lib.stat.cmu.edu`, which returns HTTP 403, so `install.packages()` got no package index and `library(redland)` then failed with `there is no package called 'redland'`:

```
Warning: unable to access index for repository http://cran.us.r-project.org/src/contrib:
  cannot open URL 'http://cran.us.r-project.org/src/contrib/PACKAGES'
```

The `librdf0-dev` apt install was working the whole time. Switched to `https://cran.rstudio.com`, which the other 46 packages already use.

## tesseract

The French check read its sample from `upload.wikimedia.org`, which answers R's curl user agent with HTTP 429 while serving plain `curl` from the same container normally — so it fails specifically through the R package, and would keep recurring. Rather than work around the user agent, both samples are now checked-in images, following the fixture pattern already used in `packages/pensieve`. The test makes no image requests at all now.

The fixtures are plain DejaVu Sans renderings generated with ImageMagick, so nothing third-party is vendored.

### Assertions

The old assertions were bare expressions:

```r
nchar(text_fra) == 3360
```

These print `TRUE` or `FALSE` but never fail the test — only an error inside `ocr()` could fail it. They are now `stopifnot()` calls.

The English check was `nchar(text_eng) == 286`, a character count tied to the specific remote image and meaningless against a different one. It is replaced by content checks covering letters, digits and punctuation.

The French assertions are not vacuous: OCRing `french.png` with only the English pack produces `éléves frangais` and `Ou étes-vous`, so both `grepl` checks fail if `tesseract-ocr-fra` is missing. Both `tesseract("eng")` and `tesseract("fra")` also error outright if the corresponding traineddata is absent, so the test still covers what it exists to cover.

Also replaced `engine = (language = "eng")` — a parenthesized assignment that just evaluates to the string `"eng"` — with the documented `tesseract("eng")` form.

## Testing

Both run against `rstudio/shinyapps-package-dependencies:jammy` locally:

- `make test-jammy-redland` — SUCCESS
- `make test-jammy-tesseract` — SUCCESS

No CHANGELOG entry: that file tracks which packages are supported and what system dependencies they need, and nothing here changes either. Happy to add one if you'd prefer.

title: Make rJava dependency install non-interactive
description:
## Summary

Add `-y` to the rJava system dependency installation so unattended image builds do not stop for apt confirmation.

## Thanks to maintainers

Thanks for maintaining these dependency scripts and for reviewing this fix.

## Issue or motivation

Closes #394. On Jammy, pending `bzip2` and `libbz2` upgrades can make the current install command ask for confirmation and abort a non-interactive build.

## Root cause

`packages/rJava/install` invokes `apt-get install` without the non-interactive `-y` option.

## Change

Pass `-y` when installing `bzip2` and `libbz2-dev`.

## Tests

- `make test-jammy-rJava`
- `bash -n packages/rJava/install`
- `shellcheck packages/rJava/install`
- `git diff --check`

The Jammy test upgraded the pending bzip2 packages, built rJava 1.0-18, initialized the JVM, and read Java version 11.0.30.

## Scope

This does not change the dependency set, the rJava functional test, the base image, or other package scripts.
